title: A credential word glued by a hyphen, dot, slash or colon to a code identifier (vault-read_token) leaves the gate classed design, not secrets
goal: a gate naming vault-read_token, registration-def_token, gitlab-bare_token, vault.read_token or vault/read_token is classed secrets, while bare_token after a space or a backtick stays classed by its other words

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import bl_authority as b; bad=[w for w in ("vault-read_token","registration-def_token","gitlab-bare_token","vault.read_token","vault/read_token") if b.class_reasons({"touches":[]},{"id":"g1","question":"Rotate "+w+" now?","options":["one","two"]})[0]!="secrets"]; print("design:",bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import bl_authority as b; c=lambda w: b.class_reasons({'touches':[]},{'id':'g1','question':'Rotate '+w+' now?','options':['one','two']})[0]; bad=[w for w in ('vault-read_token','registration-def_token','gitlab-bare_token','vault.read_token','vault/read_token') if c(w)!='secrets']+[w for w in ('bare_token','`bare_token`') if c(w)=='secrets']; print(bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
